channel.description: Latest articles from Andalusia Star News (andalusiastarnews.com)

item.title: Jail Report from January 27 to January 29
item.description: Covington County Jail report lists Jan. 27–29 arrests, including harassment, DUI, probation violations, failure to appear, and chemical endangerment of a child, with bonds up to $250,000.

item.title: Opp High School hires Sanders as football coach
item.description: Opp High School graduate Les Sanders, an experienced Alabama high school coach and current Bobcats defensive coordinator, is named athletic director and head football coach.

item.title: ACS implements secure perimeter procedure Jan. 29
item.description: Threatening call prompts secure perimeter at Andalusia schools; police respond, classes continue, and campuses return to normal as investigation proceeds.

item.title: First Responder Spotlight: Turman
item.description: Covington County Sheriff Blake Turman seeks a third term, highlighting transparency, tech upgrades and inmate rehabilitation that he credits with improving the county’s crime rating.

item.title: Britt recognizes national school choice week
item.description: Sen. Katie Britt, Sen. Bill Cassidy and 27 GOP colleagues introduce a resolution recognizing Jan. 25–31 as National School Choice Week, underscoring their push for expanded educational freedom.

item.title: Andalusia Health offers medical scholarships
item.description: Andalusia Health Services is accepting health-care scholarship applications from Covington County residents for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027. Apply by March 31, 2026.

item.title: County Youth Groups unite
item.description: More than 500 Covington County students and leaders gathered at Andalusia High School for the 2026 United Youth Conference to worship, study Scripture and reflect on identity in Christ.

item.title: Hines leads Bobcat basketball in 1,000 point career
item.description: Opp High senior DJ Hines tops 1,000 career points and powers the Bobcats’ 20-5 season, capped by a 40-point buzzer-beater in their first win over Andalusia since 2003.

item.title: WRESTLING UP FUN
item.description: Andalusia’s first youth wrestling team, now a nonprofit, is sending every member to upcoming competitions while teaching discipline, resilience and confidence.
